channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Back seats aren't as safe as they should be. A crash test is trying to help
item.description: Better engineering has made the front seat much safer in head-on collisions. But the back seat hasn't kept pace. It's a problem one vehicle safety group is trying to solve.

item.title: 'Infinite Jest' turns 30. We revisit David Foster Wallace's NPR Interview
item.description: Author David Foster Wallace published his book 'Infinite Jest' in February 1996. One year later, Wallace spoke with NPR's Tom Vitale about his literary journey.

item.title: GPB evening headlines for February 3, 2026
item.description: Georgia lawmakers debate how to regulate data centers. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard tells lawmakers she attended a raid at Fulton County election office at President Trump's request.

item.title: Syria, once home to a large Jewish community, takes steps to return property to Jews
item.description: A Jewish heritage foundation has set out to help restore private property appropriated after Syrian Jews left the country.

item.title: China bans hidden car door handles, which can trap people after crashes
item.description: China has introduced new regulations, starting in 2027, requiring all car doors to open manually from both sides. Electric door handles can malfunction in a crash or battery failure.

item.title: Despite a 'ruptured' knee ligament, Lindsey Vonn says she will compete in the Olympics
item.description: The 41-year-old's remarkable comeback from retirement was thrown into jeopardy after she hurt her knee during a crash in competition last week. But that won't keep her from racing in the Olympics.

item.title: Here's why people say they're using 'Are You Dead?' and apps like it
item.description: Safety check-in apps — a way for loved ones to know that you're alive — have become more popular among adults who feel that modern life has made connection and community more difficult to maintain.

item.title: Disney names Josh D'Amaro as its new CEO
item.description: D'Amaro will take over next month from Bob Iger, who has led the company for nearly two decades.

item.title: Brothers of Renee Good call for action in Congress
item.description: The brothers of Renee Good, killed by federal immigration officers in Minneapolis, called on Congress to do something about the violence on American streets as a result of immigration operations.

item.title: Penny the Doberman pinscher wins the 150th Westminster dog show
item.description: A Doberman pinscher named Penny won best in show Tuesday night at the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show, netting U.S. show dogs' most coveted prize.
